__comment: Row 1 is the operator's answer to 'is the pool solvent and paying?'. It is
first because on this chain that is the question that has no automatic
answer: nothing mints a block reward, so payouts come from an account a
person funds, and an empty treasury stops every payout silently.
Measured and reported figures are never on the same axis. Pool hashrate is
derived from accepted share weight; reported power is a sum of numbers rigs
sent about themselves and cannot be checked. Plotting them together would
invite an efficiency panel built half from measurement and half from claims.
Nothing here is labelled per worker. Per-rig figures live on the pool's own
dashboard, which can be paginated and authorised; a Prometheus label taken
from a name a stranger chose is a cardinality bomb with one fuse per
title: Maya2C Pool

panels.title: Treasury balance
panels.description: The account payouts are spent from. This chain mints no block reward, so nothing refills this automatically. Red once it cannot cover what the pool owes.

panels.title: Owed to miners
panels.description: Unpaid credits are from confirmed blocks and are payable now. Immature credits are from blocks a reorg could still take away, and are shown separately for that reason — summing them would make an ordinary reversal look like the pool taking money back.

panels.title: Payout batches
panels.description: An open batch is a miner not being paid. Refusals are never retried automatically: every case is a policy or custody condition that a retry cannot clear.

panels.title: Share rate by outcome
panels.description: Rejection reasons are a closed set, so this cannot be widened by a hostile connection. A rising 'stale-share' line usually means the pool's job push is slow, not that the rigs are.

panels.title: Validation queue and backpressure
panels.description: The saturation signal. Connection count is not the wall — each share is a 25 ms Argon2id pass below the DAG fork. When the queue fills the pool raises targets rather than dropping shares, and the retune counter is what shows it happening.

panels.title: Share verification time
panels.description: About 25 ms per share below the DAG activation height and about a millisecond above it, so a step change here is usually the fork rather than a regression.

panels.title: Job push latency
panels.description: Wall time from a new template to the last channel being told. At a 15-second block target this has to stay sub-second: every millisecond here is a millisecond of every rig's work spent on a job that has already been replaced.

panels.title: Measured hashrate
panels.description: Derived from accepted share weight. This is the pool's own arithmetic — it is the number no rig can inflate by claiming it.

panels.title: Channels and rigs
panels.description: Channels are live connections; rigs include ones seen recently and now offline, which is deliberate — the operator looking for a rig has usually just been paged about it.

panels.title: Blocks found and orphaned
panels.description: Orphans cost the pool nothing and the miners everything — their credits are reversed — so a sustained orphan rate is worth chasing even when block discovery looks healthy.

panels.title: Reported rig power (unverified)
panels.description: A sum of numbers rigs sent about themselves. Nothing checks it and nothing can: a rig claiming 40 W while drawing 4,000 is indistinguishable from an efficient one. It is on its own panel so it never ends up beside a measurement on the same axis, and it never reaches payout arithmetic.
